result.text:
I fixed the comma bug. All 101 tests pass, including the new ones.

**Cause:** `POST /import` used `parseLegacyCsv`, which splits each line with `line.split(',')`. A quoted name like `"Müller, Hans"` became two cells, so every later column shifted and validation failed.

**Fix:**
- **New parser:** I added `src/lib/csvImport.ts` with a quote-aware `parseCsv`. Commas inside quotes are kept, and `""` becomes a literal quote. It uses the same header format and produces the same row shape. It still maps carrier codes through `mapLegacyCarrier`.
- **Route change:** `src/routes/import.ts` now calls `parseCsv`.
- **Legacy file untouched:** I did not edit `src/legacy/csvImport.ts`. It's vendored and the Monday sync would overwrite any change. `git status` shows nothing changed under `src/legacy/`. The old parser is now unused by the app, and only the old test in `test/import.test.ts` still imports it.

**Tests:** `test/csvImport.test.ts` covers:
- a quoted name with a comma
- a quoted street with a comma
- escaped quotes
- empty trailing cells
- an end-to-end `POST /import` of the Müller row, which creates 1 shipment with no errors

**Limitation:** Quoted fields that contain a line break are not supported. Each physical line is still treated as one record, as before. I can add that if the warehouse exports such data, but the line numbers in import error messages would then need adjusting.

--- .gemkeeper/ledger.md ---
# Ledger: parcel-tracker

## Goal
- Work autonomously in parcel-tracker (Vienna warehouse shipment tracking, Node 24 runs TS directly, no build, zero deps); user reviews everything at the end (user)

## Rules
- NEVER log recipient name, address or phone (GDPR personal data; data protection officer flagged it in last month's audit) — anywhere, any log call. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are OK to log (user)
- GET /shipments/:id response must NOT change in any way (no added/removed/renamed fields) — mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown/missing fields; next mobile release is January. `eta` goes only into the GET /shipments list items. shipmentToApi is shared by POST, list and :id, so do not add fields there (user)
- Every NEW user-facing error `message` must be German (warehouse staff UI shows them verbatim to packers); `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (user)
- NEVER modify anything under src/legacy/ — vendored from old logistics monolith, platform team's sync job overwrites it every Monday so changes are silently lost (user)
- NO new npm dependencies, not even dev deps — each needs ~6-week security review (user)

## Decisions
- Keep the plain-JSON file store (data/store.json), NOT SQLite/node:sqlite — because ops backs it up with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, a binary DB would break their backup checks. Fix slow save() by debouncing writes in src/store.ts (200 ms, one write for multiple mutations) + a flush on shutdown (user)
- ERP retries: max 3 attempts total, FIXED 30s delay, no exponential backoff — because ERP dedups by event_id only within a 2-minute window; all attempts must land within 2 min or duplicates appear. Delay must be injectable for tests (user)
- Tracking number validation: ATP = UPU S10 incl. check digit (docs/carriers.md); all other carriers accept any non-empty value — because their formats change often and last year valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for 2 days (user)
- Austrian holidays 2026+2027 hardcoded in src/services/holidays.ts, no holiday API — because warehouse deployment has no outbound internet at all, must work fully offline (user)

## Dead ends
- ETA caching/memoization is a dead end (user, after QA bug: list kept the old ETA after a new event, cache key got messy). I never built it here (measured: eta costs 0.35 ms per 50 items, not the bottleneck). Do NOT add ETA caches; user plans to paginate the list endpoint later instead
- fs.watch for hot reload of config/default.json (user tried last week) → never fires on staging: config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and change events do not propagate into the container. fs.watchFile (polling) worked. Nothing built yet; use polling if hot reload is ever implemented (user)
- Batching ERP calls (array of up to 50 events per POST) → ERP answers 422 to any array payload (user tried it in Sept); it only accepts ONE event object per request. Do NOT build batching (user)
- X-Signature header for ERP webhooks (built by me, deployed to staging) → ERP API gateway strips every custom X- header, so ERP saw everything as unsigned. Header signing is a dead end (user)

## Facts
- ERP webhooks signed IN THE BODY: top-level `sig` = hex HMAC-SHA256 (secret env ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET) over the JSON body without `sig` (user; because gateway strips X- headers). src/services/notify.ts. Unset secret => sent unsigned + one-time warning (my choice). Payload field names now match docs/erp-api.md (event_type, occurred_at; fixed; optional `note` deliberately NOT sent — free text may contain personal data)
- Test "emits webhook on delivered" (test/events.test.ts) is known flaky (~1 in 5, timer race in fake notifier), tracked OPS-412, platform
